sense: to or on the other side of

terms.gloss: across, over, on the far side of
evidence: Catull. 11.9: sīve trāns altās gradiētur Alpēs
Cic. Att. 12.19.1: trāns Tiberim hortōs aliquōs parāre
terms.comment: Going across, or lying on the far side: trāns Tiberim, across the Tiber. For “opposite”, across the street from, see opposite.

terms.grammar: verb, irregular (like eō), with the accusative
terms.comment: Latin often puts “across” in the verb and the thing crossed in the accusative: flūmen trānsīre, cross the river; trādūcere, take across; trānāre, swim across.

phrases.english: or whether he marches across the high Alps

phrases.latin: cōgitō interdum trāns Tiberim hortōs aliquōs parāre
phrases.english: I sometimes think of getting a garden across the Tiber

phrases.latin: spēs ūnica imperiī populī Rōmānī L. Quīnctius trāns Tiberim … quattuor jūgerum colēbat agrum
phrases.english: the one hope of the Roman people’s empire, Lucius Quinctius, was farming a field of four iugera across the Tiber
when they are about to cross a river, they send the smallest ahead
